title: Guru Nanak founds Sikhism
place: Talwandi (present-day Nankana Sahib, Pakistan) and Kartarpur
summary: Guru Nanak, founder of Sikhism and first of the ten Sikh gurus, taught Ik Onkar ('One God'), who dwells in all creation, and a life of honest work and equality. At Kartarpur he built a community with shared meals (langar).
why: Founded Sikhism; he chose a disciple, Guru Angad, not his sons, as successor, starting the line of gurus.

notes.problem: Source glosses Ik Onkar as 'One God' who dwells in every creation; 'one divine presence' paraphrase drifts.
